newsitem.title: BURMA: Remnant Mon rebels surrender to Burma military.
newsitem.headline: Remnant Mon rebels surrender to Burma military.

text.p: Remnant Mon guerrillas, who broke away from the mainstream New Mon State Party (NMSP) when it made peace with Burma's military junta last year, have surrendered, a government statement said on Tuesday.
The breakaway group, called the Beik Mon Army, had traded in their arms to the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) on May 31 in return for a truce, the statement to Reuters said.
"The group of (150) men headed by battalian commander Aung Thaik Hym handed over 470 assorted arms to the local (Burmese army) commander," it added.
Aung Thaik Hym was the leader of some 300 armed guerrillas who broke away from the NMSP when Mon rebel leader Naing Shwe Kyin made peace with the SLORC in November.
Aung Thaik Hym and his rebels had been fighting Rangoon for greater autonomy for their southern Mon state.

"The Beik Mon Army has brought in 90 family members together with them and the remaining 150 men in arms and 700 family members stationed across the border (with Thailand) are expected to follow suit," the statement said.
The small and inactive NMSP is one of 14 ethnic Burmese rebel factions that have agreed to a ceasefire with SLORC since 1989, the statement said.
